drivers.variant_notes: segames.c builds every South Park driver from one init_sprk (INITGAME(sprk, GEN_WS, se_dmd128x32, 0): no auxiliary board) and the same de_mSES1 machine driver, so the controller routing, lamp columns and display are identical; CPU 0.90 (spkcpu.090) with display 0.90 (spdspa.090) and the 0.90 sound set, the earlier prototype IPDB lists as 'Prototype (Swearing) Roms (.90)'. No fast-flip byte, so public 15 never rises. Not exercised: the authorized ROM archive's sprk_090 set carries spdspa.101 in place of spdspa.090, so it does not load as the driver declares it.

segames.c builds every South Park driver from one init_sprk (INITGAME(sprk, GEN_WS, se_dmd128x32, 0): no auxiliary board) and the same de_mSES1 machine driver, so the controller routing, lamp columns and display are identical; CPU 0.96 (spkcpu.096) with display 1.01 and the 0.90 sound set, a prototype IPDB lists as 'Prototype (Swearing) ROMs - (.96 - More completed animations)'. MACHINE_INIT(se) sets no fast-flip byte for it, so public 15 never rises; the gameplay harness run otherwise drew the same switch-to-coil responses as sprk_103.

segames.c builds every South Park driver from one init_sprk (INITGAME(sprk, GEN_WS, se_dmd128x32, 0): no auxiliary board) and the same de_mSES1 machine driver, so the controller routing, lamp columns and display are identical; CPU 1.03 (spkcpu.103) with display 1.01 and the 1.00 sound set: the production firmware the retained table loads (cGameName = "sprk_103"). MACHINE_INIT(se) gives only this set the fast-flip byte at CPU RAM 0x00, so only sprk_103 publishes the game-on state at public 15; the harness runs saw it rise when a ball was served and fall at the drain.

(End-of-Stroke)), wired GRY-YEL to CN6-P6 on IC U206's inputs and returned to ground (BLK, CN6-P1/-P11). se.c's dedswitch_r swaps PinMAME's flipper column into U206's order and returns the complement, so public 1 is a closed contact. mechanisms.behavior: Five balls rest in the trough (500-6318-25) on micro switches 10 (left), 11, 12 and 13 and on the VUK opto 14 at the up-kicker. Q1 kicks the ball on 14 up past the stacking opto 15 into the shooter lane, and the rest roll one place toward the up-kicker. Hold each occupied position at 1 and pass the kicked ball through 15 as a short 1 pulse (beam blocked). In the gameplay runs the ROM fired Q1 repeatedly on Start until the served ball left the trough. The retained table's bsTrough omits 15.
mechanisms.label: 5-ball trough with up-kicker and stacking opto

mechanisms.behavior: A served ball rests on shooter-lane switch 16. The player plunges it with the ball shooter (500-6146-00-04), or Q2 fires the autoplunger arm (coil assembly 500-6092-02, arm 500-6091-00). The retained table fires its Plunger object with Autoplunger set.
mechanisms.label: Ball shooter and auto launch

mechanisms.behavior: The VUK Assembly (Right Style) 500-6290-01 at the top of the playfield: a ball from the left orbit (47) settles on 46 and Q4 lifts it onto the top wire ramp, which feeds the left ramp (Left Ramp Assembly page: 'ball enters from top wire ramp via VUK'). In the sprk_103 gameplay run the ROM flashed Q30 when the ball arrived and fired Q4 once some seconds later; sprk_096 fired Q4 only during a later step.
mechanisms.label: Top VUK behind the upper loop

mechanisms.behavior: The Under-Trough Assembly 500-6385-00-71 collects balls from under the toilet (43), from under Kenny (44) and from the playfield hole above the super VUK (48), each passing one micro switch, and leads them to the Super VUK Assembly 500-6184-04-71, where the ball rests on 45 until Q3 (24-940) kicks it up onto the playfield. In the gameplay runs a ball held on 45 drew repeated Q3 kicks, and one closure of 44 or 48 with the super VUK empty drew one Q3 kick, so the ROM fires the super VUK on the under-trough switch without waiting for 45; a closure of 43 alone drew none. The retained table pulses 43, 44 and 48 from kickers and hands the ball to its SuperVuk ball stack 1.2-2.4 s later.
mechanisms.label: Super VUK and under-trough

mechanisms.behavior: Toilet & Frame Assembly 500-6360-00-71. Q5 (23-1100, Toilet Lid Lift Coil Assy 500-6392-00-71) lifts the seat lid while energized; with the lid up the ball can enter the toilet, drop to the under-trough switch 43 and go on to the super VUK, and with it down the right ramp's ball passes over the toilet into the left ramp (Left Ramp Assembly page). Mr. Hankey and the tank lid ride the Mr. Hankey & Tank Lid Lift Coil Assy 500-6391-00-71: Q13 (23-1100) pulls them down onto a spring-loaded latch (trip coil assembly 515-6985-00), and Q6 (29-1000) trips it so the spring throws Mr. Hankey up. There is no position switch. In the harness runs Q13 pulsed twice at power-up and once at the drain; no run fired Q5 or Q6. The retained table raises its ToiletFlipper and enables ToiletKicker while Q5 is on, raises MrHankeyFlipper/CisternFlipper on Q6 and lowers them on Q13.
mechanisms.label: Toilet with seat lid and Mr. Hankey

mechanisms.behavior: Kenny Assembly 500-6358-00-71: Kenny stands on a carriage that two 24-940 coils swing left (Q19) and right (Q20), and the centre 22-1080 coil (Q14) pivots him over ('dead'). A #555 bulb (lamp 30) and the #906 flasher bulb (Q30) are inside the figure. The Kenny opto 42 (OPTO & Bracket (Long) Assembly 500-6242-02-71) sees the ball reach him. In the gameplay runs one 42 closure made the ROM fire Q14 once, alternate Q19 and Q20 seven pulses each, and flash Q30. Balls that reach him drop to the under-trough switch 44. The retained table rotates its Kenny primitive from the three coils.
mechanisms.label: Kenny figure

mechanisms.behavior: Left (500-5944-14) and right (500-5944-04) flipper assemblies with 23-1100 coils on one 50v supply. The CPU applies a 40 ms pulse on a button closure and then 1 ms every 12 ms while the button is held; each N.C. end-of-stroke switch opens at full stroke, and a closure during a hold earns another 40 ms pulse. PinMAME publishes Q15 at 47/48 and Q16 at 45/46.
mechanisms.label: Lower flippers

mechanisms.behavior: Left (Q9/49), right (Q10/50) and bottom (Q11/51) turbo bumpers (515-6459-01, -04, -03) with stack-blade spoon switches 180-5015-03; each switch fired its own coil in the gameplay runs, with the four pop flashers (Q7).
mechanisms.label: Three turbo bumpers

mechanisms.behavior: Left (Q12/59) and right (Q17/62) slingshots (500-5849-01), two parallel blade contacts per side; each switch fired its own coil in the gameplay runs.
mechanisms.label: Slingshots

mechanisms.behavior: UK only: Q21 and Q22 drive the left and right outlane ball deflectors (500-5788-03, coil 28-1050) and Q23 the up/down post between the flippers (500-6293-00, coil 23-1100), all on the main I/O board. The UK-only Sav-A-Ball cabinet buttons on 1 and 8 ask the ROM for them; the ROM, not a wire, raises the deflectors. A standard machine fits none of it.
mechanisms.label: UK Sav-A-Ball outlane deflectors and up/down post

Coils Detailed Chart Table (DR. 6) row #16 "RIGHT FLIPPER (50v RED/YEL)": drive transistor Q16, cell "23-1100 / 090-5030-00T". Physical Q16 is removed from public 16: se.c's se_solenoid_w masks it off and publishes it as the lower-right flipper power bit 45, and core.c synthesizes canonical callback 46 from it. Bind this one coil to public 46, the retained table's SolCallback(sLRFlipper); public 45 is its power-phase state, not a second coil. The 2-Flipper Circuit Wiring Diagram describes the drive: a 40 ms pulse on a button closure, then 1 ms every 12 ms while held, from one 50v supply through a 3A slow-blow fuse under the playfield (BLU-YEL). Placement from the retained table's Flipper FlipperRight.

physical.notes: One G.I. relay on the I/O Power Driver board 520-5137-01 (U206 data latch D0 through R254 and Q200 2N3904, coil on 20v DC with D229 across it) switches the 6.3v AC G.I. supply from J14 to four separately fused circuits on J15 (General Illumination Circuit Detailed Wiring Diagram, printed page 83): B, F24, BRN-WHT to WHT-BRN, Left Playfield & Rt. Outlane, 7 #44; Y, F25, YELLOW to WHT-YEL, Top Lt. & Rt. Playfield, 9 #44; G, F26, GREEN to WHT-GRN, Rt. P/F & Lt. Outlane + Coin Door, 6 #44 plus 2 #555 on the coin door; V, F27, VIOLET to WHT-VIO, Mid Lt. & Rt. Playfield, 9 #44. The page warns that G.I. bulb quantities may change during production. The quantity 33 is the printed 31 playfield bulbs plus the two coin-door bulbs. se.c publishes the relay as GI 0, and the harness runs saw it switch on in attract mode and blink with the outlanes and the right ramp exit. The retained table does not bind GI 0: its GIOn/GIOff/GiBlinking subs (lines 1098-1130) follow table events. Its GI collection reduces to 32 sockets once each Gi/Gis rendering pair is merged: 28 pairs, one lone light at the upper left (Gis26) and three lights inside the turbo bumpers (Gis11-13), against the 31 playfield bulbs the page prints. They are placed as the playfield bulbs, observed only; the mirrored bottom-view drawing gives no per-string assignment. The two coin-door bulbs are counted but not placed.
